part_title: Navy Regulations Part I: Naval Governance, Command Hierarchy & Appointments

articles.title: Supreme Command & Admiralty Jurisdiction
articles.text: The executive command of the Indian Navy is vested in the Chief of the Naval Staff subject to the overall direction of the President of India and Ministry of Defence.

articles.title: Command Powers of Flag Officers
articles.text: Flag Officers Commanding-in-Chief of Naval Commands exercise full administrative and operational control over all naval forces, bases, and establishments within their maritime theatre.

articles.title: Commanding Officer's Prerogatives
articles.text: The Commanding Officer of a Commissioned Warship represents the sovereign authority of the Republic of India on the high seas and maintains absolute command over all personnel embarked.

part_title: Navy Regulations Part II: Discipline, Court Martial & Naval Law

articles.title: Maintenance of Good Order & Naval Discipline
articles.text: All officers and sailors shall strictly uphold the standards of martial discipline and obedience to lawful commands under the Navy Act 1957.

articles.title: Summary Disposal Powers
articles.text: Commanding Officers possess statutory powers to summarily investigate and punish minor service offenses within prescribed tables of punishment.

articles.title: Courts Martial Procedure
articles.text: Trial by Court Martial shall be convened by a competent convening authority for grave military offenses, ensuring due process and fair legal representation.

part_title: Navy Regulations Part III: Ship Navigation, Safety & Seamanship Standards

articles.title: Safety of Ship & Navigation Protocol
articles.text: The Commanding Officer and Officer of the Watch (OOW) are jointly responsible for the safe navigation of the vessel in accordance with International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs).

articles.title: Damage Control & Fire Readiness
articles.text: Every naval vessel shall maintain continuous State-1 or State-2 damage control readiness, with weekly drills for firefighting, toxic gas containment, and flood control.

articles.title: Log Books and Official Records
articles.text: The Ship's Log Book is an inviolable statutory record and all navigational, meteorological, and operational entries must be recorded contemporaneously without erasure.

part_title: Navy Regulations Part IV: Material Administration, Store Accounting & Dockyard Procedures

articles.title: Custody & Accounting of Public Property
articles.text: Naval Supply Officers and Heads of Departments are personally accountable for the preservation, accounting, and annual stock audit of government stores in their charge.

articles.title: Dockyard Refit Protocols
articles.text: Warships entering Naval Dockyards for Scheduled or Emergency Refits shall adhere to standard work-package handover protocols, safety isolation, and quality sign-offs.

articles.title: Survey Boards and Condemnation of Stores
articles.text: Unserviceable or life-expired material shall be formally inspected by a designated Survey Board before sanction for write-off or disposal by the CFA.
